paper_title: Introducing a Phenyl End Group in the Inner Side Chains of A-DA'D-A Acceptors Enables High-Efficiency Organic Solar Cells Processed with Nonhalogenated Solvent
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2023 - Wu - Introducing a Phenyl End Group in the Inner Side Chains of A‐DA D‐A Acceptors Enables/auto/Advanced Materials - 2023 - Wu - Introducing a Phenyl End Group in the Inner Side Chains of A‐DA D‐A Acceptors Enables.md

knowledge_points.content: Two new A-DA'D-A type small molecule acceptors, Y6-Ph and L8-Ph, were synthesized by replacing the branched alkyl inner side chains of Y6 and L8-BO with phenyl-alkyl side chains containing a phenyl end group.
knowledge_points.evidence: two new small molecule acceptors (SMAs) Y6-Ph and L8-Ph are synthesized by introducing a phenyl end group in the inner side chains of the SMAs of Y6 and L8-BO, respectively

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cells based on PM6:L8-Ph processed with the nonhalogenated solvent o-xylene (o-XY) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.40% and a fill factor (FF) of 80.11%.
knowledge_points.evidence: L8-Ph-based OSCs processed by nonhalogenated solvent o-xylene (o-XY) achieved a high PCE of 18.40% with an FF of 80.11%.

knowledge_points.content: A large-area organic solar cell (1 cm²) using the PM6:L8-Ph blend processed with o-xylene achieved a power conversion efficiency of 16.66%.
knowledge_points.evidence: an outstanding efficiency of 16.66% was achieved for 1 cm2 area OSC with o-XY-processing.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of phenyl-alkyl inner side chains in Y6-Ph and L8-Ph reduces molecular crystallinity, evidenced by lower melting points (Tm) of 248 °C and 283 °C respectively, compared to 299 °C for Y6 and 321 °C for L8-BO.
knowledge_points.evidence: The melting point (Tm) of Y6, L8-BO, Y6-Ph, and L8-Ph are 299, 321, 248, 283 °C... these results indicate that the phenyl-alkyl inner side chains can decrease the molecular crystallinity

knowledge_points.content: The phenyl end group in the side chains provides steric hindrance that prevents rapid over-aggregation in slow film-forming processes while facilitating more ordered J-type aggregation through aryl-aryl interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: the phenyl end group in the inner side chains... leads to 5-10 nm blue shift... due to the steric hindrance... the phenyl-alkyl side chains may provide more abundant intermolecular interaction to modulate the molecules to form more ordered packing.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO and LUMO energy levels of Y6-Ph (-5.70/-4.04 eV) and L8-Ph (-5.67/-3.91 eV) remain identical to their parent molecules Y6 and L8-BO, indicating the phenyl end group does not affect frontier orbital levels.
knowledge_points.evidence: The EHOMO/ELUMO values of Y6-Ph and L8-Ph are -5.70/-4.04 eV and -5.67/-3.91 eV respectively, which is exactly the same as those of their corresponding SMAs of Y6 and L8-BO.

knowledge_points.content: Standard SMAs like Y6 and L8-BO exhibit a dramatic drop in PCE when processed with chlorobenzene (CB) compared to chloroform (CF) due to excessive phase separation caused by the longer film-forming time of the high-boiling-point solvent.
knowledge_points.evidence: Y6- and L8-BO-based OSCs exhibit a dramatic drop in PCE from CF- to CB-processed devices owing to the large phase separation

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis indicates that Y6-Ph and L8-Ph blend films processed with chlorobenzene maintain higher normalized integrated intensity of π-π stacking compared to Y6 and L8-BO, signifying more ordered molecular packing.
knowledge_points.evidence: Y6-Ph and L8-Ph-based films show higher normalized integrated intensity of the π-π stacking than Y6 and L8-based ones under the CB processed condition, which indicates that phenyl-alkyl inner side chains can effectively improve the molecular ordering

knowledge_points.content: The PM6:L8-Ph blend processed with chlorobenzene achieves a highly balanced charge transport with a hole-to-electron mobility ratio (μh/μe) of 1.08, compared to 2.04 for the PM6:L8-BO blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: the improved μe, μh and more balanced μh/μe for the PM6:L8-Ph blends (1.08 for L8-Ph vs 2.04 for L8-BO) were obtained.

knowledge_points.content: Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) spectroscopy shows that PM6:L8-Ph films exhibit faster hole transfer and slower non-geminate recombination compared to PM6:L8-BO films.
knowledge_points.evidence: L8-Ph exciton signal decays faster than L8-BO exciton due to its higher hole transfer rates... non-geminate recombination is found to be much slower in the PM6:L8-Ph blends than the PM6:L8-BO blends

knowledge_points.content: Y6-Ph and L8-Ph demonstrate high thermal stability with 5% weight loss temperatures (Td) of 317.8 °C and 328.3 °C, respectively, which is suitable for organic solar cell applications.
knowledge_points.evidence: Y6-Ph and L8-Ph exhibit decomposition temperatures with 5% weight loss at 317.8 and 328.3 °C respectively, which are high enough for the application as photovoltaic materials

knowledge_points.content: The optimal morphology of L8-Ph based devices processed with o-xylene is characterized by a smooth surface with an RMS roughness of 1.18 nm and homogeneous phase separation.
knowledge_points.evidence: L8-Ph-based blend films processed by o-XY present a smooth surface with an RMS of 1.18 nm... homogeneous phase separation can also be observed in the TEM images
